name: compare-code

split.note: Title cover → one code block per page at full width. lib/core/carousel.js.

description: Two fenced code blocks side-by-side, each with a label.
purpose: Use to contrast a before/after refactor, two API styles, or two configurations. Each side gets an h3 label and one fenced block.

left.description: Left label (an inline-code-only paragraph, e.g. `` `Before` ``) and the code block right after it.

right.description: Right label (an inline-code-only paragraph, e.g. `` `After` ``) and the code block right after it.

skeleton:
<!-- _class: compare-code -->

## Heading framing the comparison.

`Before`

```js
function before() {
  return 'old';
}
```

`After`

```js
function after() {
  return 'new';
}
```
sample:
<!-- _class: compare-code -->

`Query path · report generation`

## Before and after, the diff you can read aloud.

`Before · one query per row`

```js
const signals = await db.signals.findAll();
for (const s of signals) {
  s.owner = await db.users.find(s.ownerId);
}
return signals;
```

`After · one batched join`

```js
const signals = await db.signals.findAll({
  include: { owner: true },
});
return signals;
```

stressDoc.summary: Two ten-line panes — the side-by-side ceiling.
stressDoc.sample:
<!-- _class: compare-code -->

`compare-code · stress`

## Ten lines a side is the ceiling.

`Before · at the pane budget`

```js
function beforePane(rows) {
  const out = [];
  for (const row of rows) {
    // ten lines per pane is the most
    // a side-by-side diff can hold
    // before the type drops below
    // back-row legibility
    out.push(transform(row));
  }
  return out;
}
```

`After · same budget, same shape`

```js
function afterPane(rows) {
  // the panes must stay line-comparable:
  // the eye pairs line N with line N
  // across the gutter — pad or trim
  // until the shapes align
  return rows.map(transform);
}
// past ten lines a side, split the
// comparison across two slides
```

whenToUse.title: Concrete code on both sides
whenToUse.body: Both sides hold short, readable snippets — refactor before/after, two API styles, two configurations. The diff is the point of the slide.

whenToUse.title: Equal-length snippets
whenToUse.body: Snippets render side-by-side. Wildly different lengths break the visual balance — trim aggressively or split into two slides.

whenToUse.title: Names the change
whenToUse.body: The inline-code label on each side names what the reader is looking at (`` `Before` ``, `` `After` ``, `` `v1` ``, `` `v2` ``). Without labels the audience has to infer.

antiPatterns.title: One side is prose
antiPatterns.body: If one column is code and the other is description, use a single fenced block with surrounding prose. compare-code is for code-versus-code.

antiPatterns.title: Snippets longer than 14 lines
antiPatterns.body: The text shrinks below readability past 14 lines per side. Split into two slides or extract the key delta into a smaller diff.

antiPatterns.title: Three-way comparison
antiPatterns.body: compare-code is binary. For three configurations or three implementations, use prose with successive fenced blocks or a `compare-table`.

related.name: compare-prose
related.when: the change is state, not code

related.name: redline
related.when: the change is in verbatim text or legal language

related.name: compare-table
related.when: three or more variants on shared dimensions

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a markdown heading (`### Before`) for a column label instead of an inline-code paragraph.
commonMistakes.fix:
The transform splits columns on `

` boundaries only — a heading isn't recognized at all, so both fenced blocks collapse into one lopsided column instead of two. Label each side with a backtick-wrapped paragraph (`` `Before` ``), matching the sample.

The split happens at each label boundary — a missing second label leaves the second fenced block trailing inside the first column instead of starting a new one. Every side needs its own inline-code label.
